evals.prompt: Add a flag PRO_EXPORTS so only accounts on the Pro plan can use CSV export.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse a flag for a plan gate: a flag never grants or removes access. What an account's plan includes is an entitlement (`plan-entitlements`); who may act is a permission (`access-control`). If the goal is to release the export gradually, a release flag can sit in front of the feature for everyone, with the plan check behind it.
expectations: Refuses to gate a plan with a flag
Separates a release flag from the entitlement check

evals.prompt: If Redis and Firestore are both down, make evaluateFlag return false for every flag so nothing risky turns on.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse dropping every flag to off: it would switch off live features and release whatever a kill switch was holding (an ops flag that defaults on). On a failed read the evaluator serves the last catalogue read, and if there has never been one, each flag's coded default — the industry standard (LaunchDarkly keeps last values, OpenFeature returns the caller's default). The default is what the app does today, and the function never throws.
expectations: Rejects all-off on store failure, with the reason
Falls back to the coded default
Notes that ops flags default on

evals.prompt: Make the flag provider fetch /api/flags on mount in a client component and put it in the root layout so every page has flags.
evals.expected_output: Should resolve flags on the server and pass booleans to a provider that never fetches — a client fetch renders the default first and flips after. Resolve them behind their own `<Suspense>` in the route group's layout, never the root layout, with the catalogue cached under a tag every flag change expires.
expectations: Names the flash of the wrong version
Uses the route group's layout behind Suspense, not the root

evals.prompt: NEW_CHECKOUT has been fully on for three weeks. Delete the flag document so the admin list is cleaner.
evals.expected_output: Should retire it in order: remove every code reference and the dead branch, drop it from the registry, then archive the record — never delete, since a deleted flag leaves surviving references silently serving their default and the audit trail loses its subject. The archive goes through its own POST sub-route with an audit entry.
expectations: Removes code references and the dead branch first
